scenes.script_line: Every workplace faces challenges. Plans change. Equipment fails. Deadlines slip. Unexpected complications arise. These difficulties are a normal part of work. They’re also how people develop judgment, resilience, and competence. But two people can face exactly the same problem and respond in completely different ways. One creates anxiety, confusion, and additional work for everyone around them.

scenes.script_line: Sometimes the difficulty is genuine. But the defining characteristic is this: More energy is spent describing the problem than finding a solution. Sometimes this comes from feeling overwhelmed. But sometimes it comes from wanting recognition. People want others to appreciate how hard they’re working and how much responsibility they’re carrying. Without realizing it, difficulty becomes a way of demonstrating importance.

scenes.script_line: The unspoken message becomes: “Look how much I’m dealing with. Surely that makes me valuable.” But the effect can be the opposite. Instead of inspiring confidence, repeated dramatization creates concern. Instead of reducing the burden on the organization, it increases it. Because now the team must manage not only the original problem, but also the unnecessary anxiety surrounding it.

scenes.script_line: But you do need to take responsibility for your response. Don’t seek admiration for how difficult your work is. Earn respect through how effectively you handle difficulty. Don’t become the person who needs everyone to know how hard things are. Become the person everyone knows they can trust when things get hard. That is the mindset of a solution owner. And that is the standard worth aspiring to.
